profile.contributions: The paper introduces a framework to quantify and mitigate LLM over-trust in derived measurements by defining DFOT and introducing five estimands (COTR, CIR, CRR, ESRM, UHR) to evaluate the reliability of derived features. limitations_open_issues: DFOT provides a common framework but does not depend on a particular reliability generator
profile.methodological_approach: The paper defines derived-feature over-trust (DFOT) as the failure in which a downstream LLM assigns such a measurement the epistemic status of a direct fact or uses it outside its valid scope. It introduces five estimands to quantify this chain: conflict over-trust rate (COTR), context-induced error rate (CIR), correct repair rate (CRR), evidence-specific repair margin (ESRM), and utility harm rate (UHR). The framework is demonstrated on 50,000 paired PPG–ECG records using ECG-to-PPG privileged distillation as an illustrative baseline and PPG-only inference.
profile.contributions: The paper introduces a framework to quantify and mitigate LLM over-trust in derived measurements by defining DFOT and introducing five estimands (COTR, CIR, CRR, ESRM, UHR) to evaluate the reliability of derived features. It demonstrates this on physiological sensing data using PPG and ECG signals.
profile.ground_truth_validity: ECG supplies training supervision and offline reference construction but is never shown to the LLM
profile.task_solvability: The paper determines if a question can be resolved with available information in each degradation condition by evaluating repair rates and error rates.
profile.statistical_analysis: The paper reports confidence intervals for all metrics, with all paired confidence intervals excluding zero. It also provides a 95% CI for UHR: −0.4 to +1.7.
